scene_description: A bright classroom or meeting room with rows of narrow dark tables, white wheeled chairs, a two-panel window, hexagon-patterned walls and two floor lamps on the right.

visible_objects.observation: Both images show the main furniture groups, rear window, patterned walls and two lamps. The reference additionally shows a dark vertical fragment at the far right edge, not apparent in the candidate.
visible_objects.image_evidence: Reference and candidate, full image; reference right edge [0.97, 0.47, 1.0, 0.83].

spatial_relations_and_orientation.observation: Tables form roughly horizontal rows with chairs facing the rear wall. The window is centered above the furniture, and both lamps are against the right wall. The candidate presents the rows much more symmetrically and frontally; in the reference the room corner and table rows recede more strongly toward the right.

proportions_and_occlusion.observation: The foreground chairs and tables occupy much more of the reference frame, with stronger overlaps and several objects cropped at the edges. The candidate furniture is smaller and more evenly spaced, leaving more visible floor and wall around the group.

materials_and_texture.observation: Both have pale hexagonal wall lines, white chair shells, dark table tops and black chair bases. The reference wall pattern is more prominent and its tables are darker; the candidate is paler and lower contrast overall. The reference floor has subtle mottling that is not as evident in the candidate.

visible_geometry.observation: Both images show rectangular tabletops on slender legs and chairs with curved shell backs and radial wheeled bases. The candidate window has two rectangular panes but a thinner, lighter-looking frame than the dark reference frame. Fine chair and table connections are less distinct in the candidate.
visible_geometry.image_evidence: Window reference [0.41, 0.17, 0.60, 0.45], candidate [0.42, 0.23, 0.58, 0.45]; furniture in lower halves.

camera_and_composition.observation: The reference is a closer, lower and more oblique view, with the window larger and room contents extending beyond the frame. The candidate is more distant and nearly head-on, showing the left boundary of the back wall and more empty floor; its window and furniture occupy smaller image regions.

lighting_and_shadows.observation: The reference has warm, conspicuous pools of light above and below both lamps and stronger furniture contrast. The candidate lighting is flatter and grayer, with much weaker lamp illumination and softer, less pronounced shadows.

objects_regions.observation: Large white shells and black caster bases span the foreground; candidate counterparts are smaller and more uniformly aligned.
Dark narrow tops overlap in a close, angled arrangement; candidate tops appear lighter and their arrangement is more distant and frontal.
A dark thick frame encloses two pale panes; the candidate window is smaller in frame and its frame looks lighter and thinner.
Two lamps stand beside the right wall; their warm light creates strong wall highlights in the reference but much weaker illumination in the candidate.
Hexagonal outlines cover pale walls; the reference has a more prominent right-hand corner, whereas the candidate exposes the left edge of the back wall and a gray area beyond it.
A narrow dark vertical object is cropped by the reference edge and has no clear counterpart in the candidate; its identity is uncertain.

most_important_visible_defects: Camera viewpoint and framing differ substantially, making the candidate furniture and window much smaller and more symmetrically arranged.
Warm, high-contrast lamp light on the right wall is largely absent in the candidate.
Candidate table surfaces and the overall scene are much lighter and flatter than the reference.
uncertainty: The images do not establish absolute room or furniture dimensions, hidden surfaces, true physical contact, or exact object counts where items overlap or are cropped. Some apparent size and spacing differences may result from viewpoint rather than geometry.
limitations: Assessment is based only on the two supplied RGB images and approximate normalized image regions; no 3D scene or hidden ground truth was inspected.
